conclusion: Therefore despair is healed only when the self, in willing to be itself, rests transparently in God.
label: Self-And-Despair
premises: The self is a synthesis that relates itself to itself.
Any misrelation in this self-relating is despair.
The self did not establish itself but rests in the power that posited it.

conclusion: Therefore faith, not comprehension, is the proper relation to the paradox.
label: Paradox-And-Offense
premises: The absolute paradox is that the eternal God has come into being in time.
The understanding cannot think this and collides with it.
This collision issues either in offense or in faith.

conclusion: Therefore, for the existing individual, truth is subjectivity.
label: Subjectivity-Is-Truth
premises: For an existing person, truth is a matter of how one relates, not merely what is related.
The highest truth available to an existing individual is an objective uncertainty held fast in inwardness.
Such appropriation is subjectivity raised to passion.

conclusion: Therefore faith involves a teleological suspension of the ethical.
label: Teleological-Suspension
premises: The ethical as the universal forbids a father to kill his son.
Yet Abraham is held justified in his readiness to sacrifice Isaac at God's command.
This is possible only if the single individual can stand, as an individual, in an absolute relation to the absolute.

reference.source: Kierkegaard (Johannes de silentio), Fear and Trembling (1843)

conclusion: Therefore speculative philosophy cannot comprehend existence, which must be lived in subjectivity.
label: Against-The-System
premises: A logical system is possible, but an existential system is not.
Existence is a continual becoming that abstraction cannot complete.
The existing thinker is therefore never finished as the system pretends to be.
